data.claim: Yes: ItemEdit plus one repeatable set param, a per-kind catalogue and <kind>.updated events cover every kind; the MCP tool already exists
data.falsifier: a bug append_body that fails, or a replay that silently drops an unknown field

data.probe_output: 16 passed (append on bug, lesson, research, decision, memory, session, schedule; MCP twin; strict fold raises on unknown field)
data.question: Can one catalogue of fields per kind drive update on every record kind and both surfaces with no new MCP tool?

tests/test_update_universal.py 16 passed; update_record writes <kind>.updated events, strict fold in core/handlers/record_update.py

chunk_findings.detail:
`_current` retrieves records by checking if `rid` is present in `st.bugs`, `st.lessons`, etc., or `st.schedules`, but `resolve` (lines 80-92) accepts a `kind:id` reference where the `kind` part is validated against `RF.ALL_KIND_NAMES`, `_data_kind(kind)`, or `"rule"`. If a user passes an arbitrary kind prefix not present in the specific hardcoded books or if `kind` and `rid` mismatch (e.g. `lesson:B1` where `B1` is a bug and not a lesson), `_current` raises a `KeyError` because `kind` is not a valid key for the lookup dictionary:
```python
        book = {
            "bug": st.bugs,
            "lesson": st.lessons,
            "research": st.research,
            "decision": st.decisions,
            "memory": st.memories,
            "session": st.sessions,
        }[kind]
```
Given input `ddflow update lesson:B1`, `resolve` returns `("lesson", "B1", "")`, and `_current` crashes with a `KeyError` when attempting to subscript the dictionary with `"lesson"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/record_update.py:108

chunk_findings.detail: A missing id is distinguished from an ambiguous one by the substring `"several"` in the error text. `resolve` builds `no such record {ref!r}`, and the caller is supposed to get `None` so `items.update` can emit its own not-found. For any id whose rendered message contains that substring (`several`, `fix-several-bugs`, …) the condition fails and the function returns `O.refused("record.updated", …)` instead of `None`. Given ref `several` and no such record, the caller never takes the not-found path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/record_update.py:update_record

chunk_findings.detail: Bare-id resolution never looks at rules, even though this module updates them when the ref is `rule:<id>`. `_candidates` scans bugs, lessons, research, decisions, memories, sessions, schedules, and defs only. A unique live rule `my-rule` with no other record of that id makes `resolve` return `no such record 'my-rule'`, and `update_record` returns `None` without calling `rule_update`. The same edit with ref `rule:my-rule` applies.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/record_update.py:_candidates

chunk_findings.detail: Fold aliases mutable event payloads into the live record. Lists are shallow-copied, but every other container is stored by identity: given `bug.updated` with `data.fields = {"context": {"text": "x"}}` (an own field allowed by the catalogue / `--set`), `setattr` binds that same dict onto the record. `rec.context["text"] = "y"` then mutates `ev.data["fields"]["context"]`, so a later replay or persisted event no longer matches what was recorded. The same leak hits a list-of-dicts field, because `list(value)` does not copy inner dicts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/record_update.py:49

chunk_findings.detail: The new `set` parameter's `cli_help` is cut off mid-sentence: `` `ddflow help update` lists each kind's ``. `ddflow update --help` therefore prints an unfinished clause and never says what is listed (accepted fields / verbs), so the flag the change adds as the only path for own-fields and list folds does not document itself.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/queue.py:524

chunk_findings.detail: `test_every_kind_has_a_catalogue_entry_with_every_op_decided` treats any truthy `kd.nearest` as covering every operation. A kind whose catalogue sets `nearest` to a non-empty string (or a dict that does not contain the op) and lists neither `title` nor `needs` in `attrs` or `declined` still passes: `op in kd.attrs or op in kd.declined or kd.nearest` is true because the third clause never checks that this `op` was decided. The suite can stay green while an op is neither accepted, declined, nor mapped to a nearest verb.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_update_universal.py:126

chunk_findings.detail: The function `_generic_fields` calls `_attr(kd, rid, "parent")` if `edit.parent` is not `None`, but never assigns the returned attribute name and value into `fields`. Given a record edit specifying `--parent some-id`, the update silently ignores the parent change, which violates the intent of universal update operations on records that accept a parent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/record_update.py:180

chunk_findings.detail: `ItemEdit.set` is stored on the dataclass and forwarded only when `st.items.get(item)` is `None`. For an id that is still a queue item, `update()` never reads `edit.set` (this file’s only new control flow is that branch, and nothing else in the change consumes `set` on the item path). Given item `T-1` present and not removed and `edit=ItemEdit(set=["severity=high"])`, the call continues into the existing item editor, drops the own-field edit, and can still return success. That contradicts the stated contract that `--set` own fields apply to every record kind, including items.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/items/_edit.py:103

chunk_findings.detail: `update_record` treats any not-found `problem` whose text contains the substring `several` as an ambiguity refusal. `resolve` builds the missing-id error as `no such record {ref!r}`, so a ref that names nothing, such as `several` or `foo-several`, yields `problem == "no such record 'several'"` (or the same with that id inside the quotes). `kind` is `""`, so `not kind and "several" not in problem` is false and the function returns `O.refused` instead of `None`. The docstring says `None` is the signal that lets `items.update` report its own missing-item result; that handoff does not happen for those ids.
chunk_findings.title: update_record

chunk_findings.detail: `coerce` strips and lowercases booleans, and list items are stripped, but an enum is compared to `str(raw)` with no strip. `split_set` also keeps the raw side of `field=value` unstripped. Input `--set severity=high ` or `--set mode=fix\n` therefore raises `severity is one of low, medium, high, critical; got 'high '` / the same for `mode`, while `--set enabled= true` succeeds. The stored value never matches `Own.choices` even though the token is a valid choice.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/record_fields.py:coerce

chunk_findings.detail: The new `set` parameter's `cli_help` is cut off mid-sentence (`lists each kind's`), so `ddflow update --help` never states what the catalogue lists. That is the string the update help claims is the shared CLI contract for `--set`; a caller who relies on `--help` cannot tell which keys are legal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/queue.py:525

chunk_findings.detail: `test_every_kind_decides_every_operation` asserts `name in text and op.replace("_", "-") in text and "Nearest verb" in text`, but `RF.refusal(kd, "X1", op)` (or whatever generates the refusal text) may return a string that does not contain the literal string `"Nearest verb"` with that exact casing, or the field name with underscores replaced by hyphens. Given an operation whose name contains underscores (e.g., `add_tags`), `op.replace("_", "-")` yields `"add-tags"`, but the refusal text generated by `item_set` or record update helpers typically uses space-separated or original names (e.g., `"add_tags"` or `"add tags"`), causing `assert` to raise an `AssertionError` during test execution.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_every_kind_decides_every_operation` asserts `name in text and op.replace("_", "-") in text and "Nearest verb" in text`, but `RF.refusal(kd, "X1", op)` (or whatever generates the refusal text) may return a string that does not contain the literal string `"Nearest verb"` with that exact casing, or the field name with underscores replaced by hyphens. Given an operation whose name contains underscores (e.g., `add_tags`), `op.replace("_", "-")` yields `"add-tags"`, but the refusal text generated by `item_set` or record update helpers typically uses space-separated or original names (e.g., `"add_tags"` or `"add tags"`), causing `assert` to raise an `AssertionError` during test execution.
